ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No. 105); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No. 35); Financial Service Providers Act 2008 (Public Act 2008 No. 97); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (Public Act 2013 No. 69); AML/CFT (Definitions) Regulations 2011; and the beneficial-ownership disclosure directives issued by the Registrar of Companies and the Financial Markets Authority. The Registrar, the Financial Intelligence Unit, Inland Revenue, and the Financial Markets Authority share UBO verification files under a government-only access model.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Either (a) Hague Apostille route: present the Certificate of Incorporation to the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs, which will issue an Apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961; or (b) Consular Legalization route: present the Certificate to the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade for pre-certification and then to the consular officer of the receiving non-Hague state; the two routes are parallel and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Using the same mutually-exclusive parallel route: apostille by New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs for Hague Convention member states; or MFAT pre-certification followed by destination consulate legalization for non-Hague states; do not apply apostille and consular legalization to the same document in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Company, authenticated by a New Zealand Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Select only one route depending on the receiving state: (A) Hague member state: notarize the signatories, then obtain an Apostille from New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs; (B) non-Hague state: notarize the signatories, then obtain MFAT consular certification and destination embassy legalization; never combine route (A) and route (B).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors and shareholders of the Company; registered copy issued by New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Determine the receiving country's convention category. For an Apostille country, the certified copy from the Companies Office goes to the Department of Internal Affairs for apostille. For a non-Apostille country, the certified copy goes to MFAT for authentication and then to the consulate of the receiving state. These routes are alternative and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered New Zealand bank through its Bank Manager / AML Compliance Officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter is issued on bank letterhead and countersigned by the bank's AML/CFT officer. For Hague states, the bank signature must be notarized and then apostilled by the Department of Internal Affairs. For non-Hague states, the bank signature must be notarized, then certified by MFAT and legalized by the receiving consulate. Only one authentication path applies to each destination document set; sequential application of apostille and consular legalization is prohibited.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Each beneficial owner, director, shareholder and senior managing official must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the New Zealand sanctions orders administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, the Financial Action Task Force high-risk jurisdictions list, and the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit's suspicious activity reporting parameters. The screening must be repeated at initial name reservation, immediately prior to incorporation, at bank account opening, and every 180 days thereafter. Enhanced due diligence for foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) requires senior management approval, source-of-funds documentation for all trust escrow transfers, and full upward tracing through intermediate corporate or trust layers until each natural-person UBO is identified at the 25% threshold. Adverse hits must be escalated to the Financial Markets Authority and a suspicious transaction report filed before proceeding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Company Name Clearance and Reservation Portal (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A New Zealand company name may be in English or te reo Maori, using the Roman alphabet, Arabic numerals, spaces and the characters &, ', /, -, and . Names must end with 'Limited' or the approved abbreviation 'Ltd' and must be neither identical nor almost identical to any existing registered name under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) legal suffix/ending; (2) distinctive primary word; (3) acceptable descriptive element; and (4) submission to a restricted-token review where a sensitive word triggers prior approval. Non-English names must be transliterated phonetically into Roman script, and the Companies Office may require an official English translation for all due diligence filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office rejects a requested name, the applicant may file a written appeal to the Registrar of Companies within 15 working days of the rejection notice, citing the specific reason for rejection under sections 22 and 23 of the Companies Act 1993. The appeal must include a cover letter, a copy of the rejection notification, the proposed name and its Roman-script transliteration, a statutory declaration explaining why the name is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing register entry, evidence of consent from any relevant Minister or regulator where a restricted token is used, and a request that the Registrar publish a reconsidered decision in the New Zealand Gazette. The Registrar will respond within 10 working days and will state the grounds in writing; if the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may apply to the District Court for judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Section 188 of the Companies Act 1993 requires a New Zealand company to have a registered office at a physical address in New Zealand where service of documents can be accepted and the public can access; a post-office box or mail-forwarding service cannot satisfy this statutory registered-office requirement. A virtual office or commercial mailbox may be acceptable for general correspondence, but Inland Revenue and the banking sector will reject it as proof of commercial substance for a Special Purpose Acquisition Company operating under ISIC 6499/NAICS 525990. The company must maintain an on-the-ground physical suite, permanent signage, corporate records, and a responsible officer or agent to receive inspections; a nominee-only virtual address will create significant tax-residency and bank account-opening risks under the Income Tax Act 2007 and the AML/CFT Act 2009.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The New Zealand Companies Office, Inland Revenue Department, and Financial Markets Authority conduct both desk and unannounced physical inspections under the AML/CFT and Companies Act frameworks. The practical checklist includes: (1) display of the company name at the registered office; (2) availability of directors and staff; (3) full accounting and UBO records; (4) signed trust escrow agreement and wire transfer logs; (5) the bank reference letter and deposit confirmation; and (6) the original register of charges and minutes. For a newly formed blank-check acquisition vehicle with a medium-risk enhanced AML profile, the probability of a physical on-site visit within the first 12 months is estimated at 60-70%; the visit is most likely to be initiated by the AML/CFT supervisor or Inland Revenue rather than the Companies Office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 10, 12, 20-22, 39-42, 126-129, 151-153, 161; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, ss 451-462; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, ss 5-12, 56-58; Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, ss 13-20.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (electronic Companies Office instrument under section 39 of the Companies Act 1993)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: New Zealand has no statutory minimum paid-up capital. A company may have nil share capital until subscription funds are received. No blocked escrow account is required for incorporation. If the SPAC executes an initial public offering or NZX listing, the offering proceeds must be escrowed under the trust deed in a segregated account until a qualifying acquisition or return of capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 (2025) — UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED. WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated under section 40 of the Companies Act 1993 of New Zealand (the 'Act') as a special purpose acquisition company for the public market acquisition, merger, amalgamation, business combination or share exchange; and WHEREAS, the initial directors are authorized to determine the governance and administrative arrangements of the Company, to subscribe for and allot shares, to appoint officers, to open bank accounts, to adopt a registered office and to take all actions necessary to commence operations. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. SHARE ISSUANCE AND SUBSCRIPTION. The initial allotment of ordinary shares, founder shares, options and warrants is approved; the directors are authorized to issue and allot such financial products upon receipt of subscription moneys, in accordance with the constitution and Parts 4 and 9 of the Act. 2. BANKING AND ESCROW. The authorization to open corporate, trust and escrow bank accounts at a bank licensed in New Zealand is granted; the Chief Executive Officer or Chief Financial Officer, together with any other director, shall have signing authority for SWIFT transfers, wire instructions and account maintenance mandates. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company is adopted as [physical registered office address], New Zealand, and the address for service is deemed fixed; any change shall be filed with the Companies Office. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The board appoints [Director A], [Director B], [Chief Executive Officer], [Chief Financial Officer], and [Company Secretary] to the offices stated, each to serve until removed by the board; the board confirms each appointee meets the fit-and-proper standards, is not disqualified under sections 151 to 152 of the Act, and consents to act. 5. GOVERNANCE AND REGULATORY AUTHORIZATION. The officers are directed to register the Company on the Financial Service Providers Register, apply for AML/CFT compliance programme approval, file tax registrations with Inland Revenue, and apply for NZX listing or other exchange admission if a public SPAC listing is pursued. 6. GENERAL DELEGATION. Any one director or the Company Secretary is authorized to execute and file all documentation, consents and statutory forms required by the Act, the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, the AML/CFT Act 2009, and applicable listing rules. This resolution is adopted as of [date] and is effective immediately upon incorporation. ADOPTED by unanimous written consent of the sole initial director(s) of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Electronic Incorporation Filing with the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), MBIE, through the online Companies Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a New Zealand Companies Office name search or reservation to confirm the name 'NZ_LTD' is available and registerable under sections 20-22 of the Companies Act 1993. Prepare a bespoke SPAC constitution containing share class rights, waiver and director investment powers. Log in to the Companies Office online register and complete the electronic application for registration by entering the proposed name, registered office, address for service, all directors, shareholders and initial capital structure. Attach any required consents, upload the constitution, verify the KYC details of each director and shareholder, and submit the electronic application with payment. The Registrar will review and issue the certificate of incorporation under section 42 of the Act if the application is compliant.
required_dossiers: Name search result or approved reservation
SPAC constitution
Completed electronic incorporation application
Full legal names, dates of birth and residential addresses of each director
Shareholder list and class rights statement
Signed consents to act as director or shareholder
Registered office and address for service details
Payment of the prescribed registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries the name, director consent or constitution, the applicant must resubmit corrected information through the online portal within 10 working days, otherwise the application is treated as withdrawn. If the name is refused, the applicant may reserve a new name or lodge a formal reconsideration request under section 21 of the Companies Act 1993. If registration is suspended due to incomplete KYC, provide notarized passport copies and proof of residential address within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and IRD Number for the SPAC Holding Vehicle
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand, through the myIR and Business Registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the certificate of incorporation and company extract, create a myIR Business account for the company with Inland Revenue. File the IR596 company registration application to obtain an IRD number. If the SPAC will make taxable supplies, register for GST; if it will employ staff, register as an employer and for KiwiSaver. Provide the company's registered office, physical business address, director and shareholder details, and bank account details for refunds. Confirm the financial year balance date for annual income tax returns and withholding payment dates. For non-resident investors, identify whether non-resident withholding tax or approved issuer levy applies to distributions, and set up RWT accounts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Companies Office extract
Company constitution
Directors' and shareholders' identity documents
Business and registered office addresses
IR596 company registration form
Bank account confirmation for Inland Revenue refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD issues a beneficial-ownership query, the company should file a completed IR595 or a director's statutory declaration explaining the SPAC ownership chain. Missing or incorrect data can be corrected through myIR without penalty if remedied before the relevant due date. Late-filing penalties may be mitigated by applying to Inland Revenue for an administrative waiver or instalment arrangement under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: FSPR Registration and AML/CFT Compliance Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office as administrator of the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; AML/CFT supervision by the Financial Markets Authority (FMA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application with the Financial Service Providers Register using the Companies Office portal, selecting the classes of financial services provided by a SPAC, including securities transactions and financial product management as applicable, and nominate a dispute resolution scheme. Concurrently prepare a written AML/CFT risk assessment of the SPAC's investors, payment rails including trust escrow and SWIFT wire, and intended acquisition counterparties. Adopt an AML/CFT compliance programme under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, appoint a compliance officer and a reporting officer, and maintain records of suspicious transaction reporting. Submit the programme and FSPR confirmation to the Financial Markets Authority where required, and notify any identified correspondent bank.
required_dossiers: FSPR online application
Certificate of incorporation
Company constitution
AML/CFT compliance programme and risk assessment
AML/CFT compliance officer letter of consent
Schedule of financial services and registration classes
Dispute resolution scheme membership confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSPR registration is rejected or marked invalid, the company may resubmit with fully completed details and pay any reinstatement fee. A formal FMA concern letter must be answered by a corrective action plan and a revised AML/CFT programme within 15 working days. The company is entitled to be heard under FMA supervision procedures before any public censure, direction or enforcement order is imposed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SPAC Trust Escrow Account Establishment and NZX Listing Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: NZX Limited (NZX Market Supervision) and a licensed independent trustee or statutory custodian licensed under the Securities Trustees and Statutory Supervisors Act 2011, in coordination with the Financial Markets Authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Negotiate and execute a SPAC trust and escrow deed with a licensed New Zealand or Australian trustee bank, establishing a segregated trust account to receive the proceeds from public investors via SWIFT wire and hold them until a qualifying business combination. Open the segregated account with a New Zealand registered bank and complete anti-money laundering customer due diligence on the SPAC and each signatory. Prepare and file a product disclosure statement with the Financial Markets Authority if financial products will be offered to the public, then submit the NZX or other exchange listing application together with escrow opinions, audited financial statements and supporting legal opinions. Ensure compliance with NZX SPAC listing rules, post-listing obligations and any required investor redemptions.
required_dossiers: SPAC trust deed and escrow agreement
Registered bank confirmation of segregated trust account
Product Disclosure Statement filed with FMA
NZX listing application package
Board resolution adopting NZX Listing Rules
Legal opinion of New Zealand counsel on SPAC structure
Advisor certificates and audited financial statements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the trustee declines the escrow mandate due to AML/KYC deficiencies, provide source-of-funds evidence, a corporate ownership chart and a board resolution. If the FMA queries the product disclosure statement, the company must lodge a supplementary disclosure document and, if necessary, suspend the capital raise until clearance. If the exchange rejects the listing application, the issuer may appeal to the NZX Appeal Committee or reapply after correcting the listing defects.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable to ISIC 6499 SPAC; the relevant regulatory authorities are the Financial Markets Authority, the Financial Service Providers Register and NZX Limited for financial market licensing. A local territorial authority and WorkSafe New Zealand would become competent only if physical premises or industrial operations are later established.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable to ISIC 6499 blank-check SPAC; the relevant authorizations are FSPR registration, FMC reporting entity status and, if listed, NZX listing approval. No physical manufacturing or operating permit is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable — Ministry for the Environment and regional councils under the Resource Management Act 1991 would be competent only if physical operations are later established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA required for a pure ISIC 6499 special purpose acquisition company with no physical premises, discharge, land disturbance or processing activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No numeric thresholds apply because no wastewater, VOCs, hazardous waste or chemical storage is generated by the SPAC vehicle. Future operating subsidiaries acquired by the SPAC must comply with the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality 2004, the National Environmental Standards for Sources of Human Drinking Water 2005, and the Hazardous Substances Notice as applicable at the time of acquisition.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. No Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection or hazardous process approval is required by the formation of an ISIC 6499 SPAC. If an administrative office is established, the company must maintain a Fire Evacuation Scheme under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017 and meet WorkSafe New Zealand obligations under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Te Tari Taake, New Zealand; electronic return and registration portal: myIR (myIR.ird.govt.nz).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an NZ Ltd incorporated under the Companies Act 1993, the Companies Office issues a certificate of incorporation and automatically notifies the IRD, which issues an IRD number. For a non-resident or foreign-incorporated entity with New Zealand taxable supplies or source income, the entity must register for an IRD number through myIR by completing the prescribed company tax registration application and providing the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, ultimate beneficial ownership schedule, New Zealand registered office or agent details, and expected New Zealand commencement date. The IRD will then issue an IRD number; the same myIR registration flow is used to apply simultaneously for GST, employer responsibilities, and other tax accounts where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under New Zealand tax law. An eligible NZ Ltd with five or fewer shareholders may elect look-through company (LTC) status under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, causing income to be attributed to shareholders; a qualifying company election is only available to pre-existing qualifying companies. Hybrid mismatch adjustments under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 apply to any double-deduction or deduction/non-inclusion outcomes across jurisdictions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, including GST on remote services supplied to New Zealand consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month rolling period; registration is mandatory once the threshold is exceeded, and voluntary registration is available for suppliers under threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance requirement, no continuous transaction control, and no anti-fraud digital stamping. E-invoicing is voluntary using the Peppol framework. GST returns and GST adjustment schedules must be filed periodically through myIR, and IRD may request the underlying electronic invoice data during an audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under sections 11 and 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, a supply is zero-rated when goods are physically exported by the supplier within 28 days of the time of supply; when goods are supplied to a non-resident for export and are exported within the statutory timeframe; or when services are supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of performance and the services are not directly enjoyed or supplied to a person in New Zealand. For an SPAC holding company, arrangement, listing-readiness and acquisition-advisory services can qualify for zero-rating only if the recipient is offshore and the benefit is not attributable to a New Zealand taxable activity; purely passive holding activities are outside the taxable sphere.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service export declaration lodged electronically through the Customs Trade Single Window (export entry record)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Commercial invoice and GST tax invoice issued in accordance with section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
Proof of export dispatch, such as packing lists, container gate records, or terminal receipts evidencing export within 28 days
Bank SWIFT or inward remittance advice evidencing payment in foreign currency or NZD from the offshore counterparty
Zero-rating working papers retained in the GST return and tax file for IRD inspection
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: There is no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline in New Zealand; the evidentiary records must be retained for seven years. If the IRD determines that zero-rating was claimed without valid export proof, the output tax is clawed back by reassessment plus use-of-money interest. Penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply by reference to the shortfall and culpability: a lack of reasonable care or an unacceptable tax position attracts a shortfall penalty of 20%; an abusive tax position attracts 50%; and evasion or a similar wilful act attracts 100%. Criminal sanctions may also apply for knowingly false declarations made to the IRD or New Zealand Customs Service.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalised and open capital and current account regime under IMF Article VIII, with the New Zealand dollar freely convertible. There is no foreign exchange control board, no central bank approval for opening foreign currency accounts, no prior authorisation for repatriation of capital, and no requirement to surrender export proceeds. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is responsible for currency issuance, prudential supervision of registered banks, and oversight of wholesale settlement systems, but it does not administer foreign exchange rationing or convertibility licences. Current account payments for trade, services, royalties, dividends, interest, and management fees may be settled freely through any authorised bank. Capital account transactions are equally unrestricted for an ordinary New Zealand holding company, except that the Overseas Investment Act 2005 imposes targeted screening for acquisition of sensitive land, fishing quota, or significant business assets by non-residents; a special purpose acquisition company formed purely as an acquisition vehicle and holding cash pending an overseas target acquisition will generally not trigger OIO consent unless the target itself involves New Zealand sensitive assets. Profit remittance is taxed according to ordinary dividend withholding rules and the fully imputed New Zealand tax system, but there are no repatriation delays, no conversion quotas, no notional central bank swap requirements, and no administrative hurdles beyond standard anti-money laundering verification. Inward capital injections and outward acquisition funding flow through the CLS-settled NZD market at commercial rates without Treasury pre-approval, subject only to the counterparty due diligence of the relevant New Zealand bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand has no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion timeline or ratio. Exporters and holding companies may retain foreign currency proceeds indefinitely, hold them in domestic or offshore foreign currency accounts, and convert them to NZD or any other freely tradeable currency at commercial rates without central bank permission.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions and non-bank payment service providers are generally permitted to operate under New Zealand's Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. They may offer payment initiation, foreign exchange conversion, and limited stored-value or wallet products. However, they are not registered banks and cannot hold demand deposits, extend lending, or provide regulated trust-escrow services that would be acceptable for a blank-check SPAC's statutory capital verification. For the initial public offering proceeds, a special purpose acquisition company must normally maintain cash and securities in a segregated client trust or escrow arrangement at a regulated New Zealand bank with strong balance sheet strength, treasury dealing capability, and SWIFT connectivity. The practical viability of a fintech EMI for the central treasury mandate is therefore low; it may only be used as an ancillary payment rail for operational expenses in selected low-risk jurisdictions, and never as the primary repository for sponsor capital or escrowed IPO proceeds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand law does not impose a blanket statutory requirement for every director to appear physically in a bank branch. Under the Companies Act 1993, a New Zealand company must have at least one director who is a natural person and who is ordinarily resident in New Zealand or in Australia, if that director is resident in Australia and is also a director of an Australian company. Banks may on-board corporate clients remotely using verified electronic identity checks, video-conference interviews, and secure online submission of authenticated documents. For a higher-risk SPAC structure, the bank's compliance committee will normally insist on a recorded video interview with the sponsor, the key economic owner, and the New Zealand-resident director, and may request a physical or consular-witnessed interview only where passport verification or beneficial-owner identification cannot be obtained digitally from a reliable independent source. Remote opening through a New Zealand registered office agent is permissible, but the bank must still verify the identity and authority of every individual who executes account mandates; in practice, a fully remote on-boarding with notarised corporate resolutions and independent director identity verification is viable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered ownership chain and unclear ultimate beneficial ownership involving offshore trusts or holding companies, creating inability to determine the true sponsor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full registered corporate extract for every entity in the ownership chain; certificate of incorporation or equivalent; trust deed, deed of retirement, and protector/settlor/beneficiary schedule for any trust; passport and proof of address for every natural person exercising at least 25 percent ownership or control; a consolidated group structure chart signed by a qualified legal adviser; and a declaration confirming no bearer shares or bearer warrants exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Blank-check special purpose acquisition company profile triggering suspicion of unlicensed securities offering, capital accumulation without a genuine acquisition mandate, or investor-fund misuse.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legally reviewed private placement memorandum or prospectus; independent legal opinion confirming the vehicle's compliance with the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 or the availability of an applicable exclusion; a binding escrow agreement with a New Zealand registered bank or NZX-acceptable custodian; detailed acquisition mandate and target sector policy; sponsor track record with completed acquisitions; and quarterly board minutes evidencing treasury review and deployment discipline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth for large sponsor contributions appears inconsistent with declared net worth, corporate revenue, or PE/PEP status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of each subscribing sponsor or shareholder for the past three fiscal years; personal and corporate tax returns; independent bank statements for at least twelve months showing the accumulation path of contributed assets; notarised sale-and-purchase contracts or dividend and liquidation receipts backing the funds; statutory declaration of source of funds; and, where a politically exposed person is involved, an independent external AML specialist report and completed enhanced due diligence questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursements to target acquisition consultants, escrow agents, or unknown counterparties in high-risk jurisdictions could indicate sanctions evasion, trade-based money laundering, or suspicious pre-acquisition payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Invoices, executed master service agreements, and closing schedules for every material payment; full sanctions screening results against United Nations, European Union, United States OFAC, and New Zealand consolidated lists; detailed SWIFT MT103 payment purpose and confirmation references; complete KYC file of each ultimate counterparty; board-approved counterparty risk rating reflecting jurisdiction, ownership, business model, and beneficial owner; and an external trade AML review confirming the commercial rationale and fair value of each transaction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital should be routed through the SGSS/CLS chain using a SWIFT MT103 payment from the sponsor's bank directly to the New Zealand bank account designated as the capital escrow account. The payment must include the company name, bank BIC, account number, and the purpose code or free-text description stating Capital contribution for subscription and allotment of ordinary shares in NZ_LTD. Since New Zealand imposes no exchange controls, the bank will convert the incoming USD/EUR/CNY into NZD at the prevailing commercial offering rate without requiring Reserve Bank approval. If the sponsor injects a convertible loan instead of equity, the bank should be given the loan agreement, intercompany resolution, and a suitability note confirming that the amount will be on-lent in compliance with ordinary thin capitalisation and withholding tax rules. The New Zealand auditor or registered chartered accountant will issue a capital verification report based on the bank statement, subscription letters, share allotment resolution, and the Companies Act 1993 register, with dividends or shareholder current accounts fully documented.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound acquisition and operational payments should be executed over SWIFT MT103 for straightforward wire transfers to the target company's principal bank, with full beneficiary bank details, remitter reference, and purpose code corresponding to the transaction. For trade settlements involving physical goods or deferred acquisition earn-outs, the New Zealand bank may issue an irrevocable commercial letter of credit in favour of the target or vendor, governable by UCP600, or use documentary collections under URC522 where the vendor accepts draft-on-documentary terms. All outbound disbursements require the board-approved payment schedule, original invoice or closing statement, sanctions pre-screening of all intermediaries, and a written compliance sign-off from the designated AML/CFT officer. Because NZD is freely usable and CLS-eligible, the bank can settle cross-currency trades using normal BIS standard reporting; any manual intervention is only required for jurisdictions with sanctions restrictions or correspondent bank limitations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable NZD-forward contracts for committed operating expenses, acquisition consideration, and capex, up to the maturity of each binding obligation, with no speculative intent
Plain-vanilla NZD/foreign-currency swaps for aligning fixed-rate funding and acquisition proceeds with expected FX cash flows

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in non-convertible emerging market currencies only where the underlying trade or acquisition commitment is denominated in that currency and the local exchange controls prohibit deliverable settlement
Vanilla FX options and option collars, where used solely to cap the cost of a legally committed cross-border acquisition exposure and approved in writing by the bank's markets compliance desk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under Companies Act 1993, Part 12
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than one calendar month after each anniversary of the company's incorporation (the annual return date); if the anniversary falls on a weekend or public holiday, the filing deadline moves to the next business day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Filing after the due date attracts a late filing fee of NZ$50.00 (approx. USD 31.00). If the Annual Return remains unfiled after the Registrar issues a notice of default, the company may be struck off the New Zealand Register after at least 20 working days' notice in the New Zealand Gazette; strike-off extinguishes the company's legal personality, with consequential loss of asset-holding capacity and potential personal liability of directors for unpaid obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report, Directors' Report and Audited Financial Statements under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 and the Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA); New Zealand Stock Exchange (NZX) if the SPAC is listed; delivered to all shareholders.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For an FMC reporting entity, no later than four months after balance date; for an NZX-listed issuer, distribution to NZX and FMA simultaneously with the market announcement and through the NZX Online portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or late filing exposes the company and every director to civil liability under the FMC Act, enforceable undertakings, FMA infringement notices, and court-imposed pecuniary penalties up to NZ$5,000,000.00 per contravention for a body corporate; NZX may further suspend trading, require prior review, or delist the special purpose acquisition vehicle, and may issue a disciplinary fine.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registered Office, Directors and Shareholders required by the Companies Office in respect of the SPAC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due at the same time as the Annual Return (anniversary date + one month), or within 10 working days of any change to directors, registered office, or allotment notification.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain accurate registers and updated particulars is a Companies Act offence; penalties include infringement fines and late filing fees. Persistent non-confirmation may trigger administrative strike-off, and the SPAC can be removed from the Register if confirmation is repeatedly not lodged.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified independent audit is mandatory for: (i) an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, which includes a SPAC that has made an offer of securities to the public or is listed on an exchange; (ii) a 'large' for-profit entity under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, defined as an entity with total assets in excess of NZ$10,000,000 at balance date or total annual revenue in excess of NZ$20,000,000; (iii) a company whose annual return shows capital or controlled assets requiring a statutory audit due to a court order or FMA direction; and (iv) any company where shareholders holding not less than 5% of the voting rights validly require an audit. The New Zealand statutory size test is balance-sheet and turnover based; there is no separate New Zealand headcount threshold that triggers an audit for a limited company, although a headcount of 50 or more employees remains a commercial indicator for group-reporting consolidation and stewardship analysis.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For a public-market SPAC, financial statements must be prepared under NZ IFRS (Tier 1 pronouncements issued by the External Reporting Board), with full general purpose financial reporting, consolidated group reporting, and an auditor's report under the Financial Reporting Act 2013. Tier 2 Reduced Disclosure Regime is available only to non-publicly-accountable large entities; a SPAC cannot adopt the Tier 3 Small/Simple Format Reporting framework because it has public accountability. All accounting records must satisfy Part 11 of the Companies Act 1993.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand maintains no separate annual UBO return form; the annual return filed with the Companies Office is the statutory annual confirmation that records the registered office, directors, shareholder schedule and ultimate holding company, and it must be accurate as at the annual return date. For shareholding transfers, the board must update the Company's Register of Members without undue delay, generally within 10 working days after lodgement, and any allotment must be notified to the Registrar within 10 working days. For an FMC-reporting SPAC, a substantial securityholder notice (5% or more of voting securities) must be disclosed to the FMA and NZX within 5 working days of the relevant acquisition or material movement. There is no 30-day UBO filing window under New Zealand law; the 30-day convention is not applicable in this jurisdiction.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Allotments and Transfers
Company interest register / related-party register under section 189 of the Companies Act 1993

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand operates a full-imputation corporate tax system with no statutory tax holidays. Key incentives for a NZ-resident SPAC: (1) resident companies pay 28% on net income including assessable interest earned by the SPAC trust escrow; (2) an R&D tax credit equal to 15% of qualifying R&D expenditure (Income Tax Act 2007, Part L); (3) unlimited tax loss carry-forward subject to shareholder continuity; (4) imputation credits attach to cash distributions, eliminating double taxation for NZ-resident shareholders; (5) the available subscribed capital rules (s CD 43) permit tax-free capital returns on redemption; (6) no general anti-deferral or tax-holiday regime is available to a blank-check vehicle.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carry-forward under s IA 5 of the Income Tax Act 2007, subject to the 49% continuity of beneficial ownership test; no 5-year statutory cap)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return), filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR online portal or IRD-approved e-filing software; supplementary International Dealings Schedule (IR402) and tax reconciliation (IR4J) are attached to the annual IR4
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (IR4), supported by three provisional tax instalments per income year for standard balance-date taxpayers and one terminal tax payment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 is due on the 7th day of the 4th month following balance date (for a standard 31 March balance date: 7 July). Provisional tax instalments for a standard balance date are due on 7 July, 7 November, and 7 May; terminal tax is due on 7 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income and turnover: report all assessable income, including interest income earned by the SPAC trust escrow account, gains on derivative instruments, foreign exchange gains, dividends received, and royalty income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The NZ-resident SPAC must report its worldwide income. Non-resident shareholders should ensure only entity-level NZ income is included; interest on the US or global escrow account is fully assessable in New Zealand regardless of where the account is custodied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses: operating costs, professional fees, NZX or overseas listing fees, directors' fees, banking and custody charges, insurance and SPAC compliance costs; interest deductions are separately capped by the thin-capitalisation safe harbour
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-controlled SPAC, interest deductions are limited to the NZ debt percentage of 60% of assets, or 110% of the worldwide group debt percentage where greater (s FE 18). Excess interest must be added back in this box with a reconciliation note.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before taxation: the accounting result as adjusted for tax purposes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Eliminate non-deductible items such as penalties, entertainment disallowances, corporate income tax itself, and deemed distributions. Imputation debit adjustments arising from redemption must also be reconciled here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses brought forward: NZ tax losses carried from prior years, allowed only where the 49% shareholder continuity test is satisfied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A change in the SPAC's shareholder register following the business combination may breach continuity and destroy the loss pool. The SPAC must attach a continuity certificate and detailed shareholder election schedules if continuity is relied on.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after the set-off of carry-forward losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot utilise NZ losses personally; all losses are trapped at the entity level. Group loss offset (s IG 1) applies only within a 100% NZ-resident corporate group.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate applied: 28% corporate rate for the 2024/25 and subsequent income years
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 28% rate applies uniformly regardless of shareholder residence. No look-through company election is available to a public-listed SPAC, and no branch-equivalent filing is accepted for a NZ-incorporated vehicle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on taxable income: the amount calculated at the Box 6 rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SPAC has subsidiaries, the tax is calculated on the consolidated group using specified grouping elections. Foreign intercompany dividends may qualify for the participation exemption under s CW 9 and are excluded from the Box 1 gross income figure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: resident withholding tax (RWT) on interest, non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) credits, imputation credits, and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: RWT deducted from escrow interest is creditable against the SPAC's own income tax. A non-resident shareholder's NRWT on dividends is not a credit against the SPAC's income tax and must not be entered in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax and terminal tax: the net amount payable by 7 April (standard balance date) or the refundable amount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any SPAC redemption or liquidation distribution that exceeds the available subscribed capital must be classified as an imputed dividend subject to 30% NRWT at the shareholder level; that NRWT is a debt of the SPAC and is not set off here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reconciliation (IR4J) and International Dealings Schedule (IR402): the IR402 discloses cross-border related-party transactions, related-party interest-bearing loans, and the arm's-length position taken
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: IR402 is mandatory when cross-border related-party transactions in goods, services, or intellectual property, or related-party loans, exceed NZD 1,000,000 in the income year. A non-resident parent must supply the loan agreements and benchmark interest rate computations supporting each related-party financing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 (small taxpayer), NZD 250 (medium taxpayer), or NZD 500 (large taxpayer) per return, with additional default assessments for each month of continued non-lodgement; late payment penalty of 1% per month on the unpaid amount; use-of-money interest (UOMI) at the prescribed corporate rate on underpayments from the due date; shortfall penalties of 20% (lack of reasonable care, s 141A), 40% (gross carelessness, s 141B), 100% (abusive tax position, s 141D), or 150% (evasion or similar, s 141E) of any resulting tax shortfall.
